title: Supercharging Transactions with Async Payjoin
description:
Level: Beginner

Payjoin is a simple, flexible, and powerful protocol for a sender and receiver to collaboratively construct Bitcoin transactions. This allows for many optimizations, such as fee savings and scaling via [batching](https://payjoin.org/docs/why-payjoin/scaling), opportunistic [UTXO consolidation](https://bitcoin.stackexchange.com/questions/103194/confused-about-utxo-management-and-consolidation), and [transaction cut-through](https://payjoin.org/docs/why-payjoin/scaling#transaction-cut-through), as well as better privacy by breaking [privacy-thieving heuristics](https://payjoin.org/docs/how-it-works/payjoin-v1-bip-78/#motivation), solving the sole privacy problem [left open in the whitepaper](https://nakamotoinstitute.org/library/bitcoin/#privacy). Payjoin *enhances transactions* without requiring any changes to Bitcoin. The magnitude of these positive effects scale with usage — the more transactions that are Payjoins, the more fee savings, blockchain throughput, and privacy for everyone.

The first version of Payjoin ([BIP-78](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0078.mediawiki)) required the receiver to run an always-online server secured by TLS or a TOR hidden service, which proved to be a [barrier to adoption](https://lists.linuxfoundation.org/pipermail/bitcoin-dev/2021-January/018358.html).

Asynchronous Payjoin*, aka Serverless Payjoin, Payjoin Version 2, or Draft [BIP-77](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/1483), outsources this problem by delegating the coordination to an untrusted third party, while also taking measures to further improve privacy and improve UX by integrating novel protocols [Oblivious HTTP](https://blog.cloudflare.com/stronger-than-a-promise-proving-oblivious-http-privacy-properties/) and [HPKE](https://blog.cloudflare.com/hybrid-public-key-encryption).

A Rust library for developing with Payjoin, [PDK](https://payjoindevkit.org/), is under active development and is rapidly iterating.

Given the recent [attacks](https://www.justice.gov/usao-sdny/pr/founders-and-ceo-cryptocurrency-mixing-service-arrested-and-charged-money-laundering) on Bitcoin privacy, the use of censorship-resistant and privacy-by-default tools are more important than ever. The time and fee savings individuals and companies can accrue serve as an additional incentive to achieve improved privacy for the whole network.

Payjoin adoption is relatively [low](https://en.bitcoin.it/wiki/PayJoin_adoption) as of today. This talk seeks to shed light on Asynchronous Payjoin as a viable low-interaction protocol for optimizing privacy, efficiency, and fee savings in Bitcoin transactions.

This talk will cover:

- Brief history of ideas relating to Payjoin (Coinjoin, P2EP, etc.)
- Brief overview of how V1 works and barriers to adoption
- Benefits of Payjoin
    - Batching
    - Transaction cut-through
    - UTXO consolidation
    - Privacy
- Overview of Asynchronous Payjoin (BIP-77)
    - UX and Privacy Improvements
    - Outsourcing communication to untrusted Payjoin Directories
    - Oblivious HTTP
    - HPKE
    - Limitations
- Demonstration with reference implementation [`payjoin-cli`](https://github.com/payjoin/rust-payjoin/tree/master/payjoin-cli)
- Possible Use Cases, such as better batching for exchanges and Lightning cut-through

 What would an attendee learn from this talk?

- How can Payjoin save money?
- How does Payjoin improve privacy?
- Payjoin has been around for a few years. Why hasn't it seen much adoption?
- Why would exchanges integrate Payjoin?
- Why would wallet developers integrate Payjoin?
- How does Asynchronous Payjoin improve over BIP-78?
- How to do an Async Payjoin on Bitcoin Core

 Is there anything folks should read up on before they attend this talk?

This talk is for anyone who is interested in Payjoin and assumes no prior knowledge. That said, here are some links that can help shed light on Payjoin prior to attending:

- [payjoin.org](https://payjoin.org/)
- [Payjoin V2](https://payjoin.org/docs/how-it-works/payjoin-v2-bip-77)
- [How Can Payjoin Save 16% on Transaction Fees?](https://payjoin.org/docs/how-payjoin-saves)
- [Payjoin for a Better Bitcoin Future](https://blu.cx/payjoin-for-a-better-bitcoin-future/)

 About the Speaker

Brandon Lucas is a frontend engineer at [Voltage](https://voltage.cloud/), working on Payjoin and other open source Bitcoin projects in his spare time. See more of his work at [blu.cx](https://blu.cx/).
